data.title: Publish what the author approves, and show what a rerun needs
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Last PR of the software provenance series. A study already keeps privately what a rerun needs (#128). This PR decides what of that leaves the machine, under the author's approval, and shows it on the dashboard.

## What a publication holds

Beside each snapshot, `k4opt publish` always writes a **software sheet** (`studies/<id>/software/<sha16>.json`, `k4opt.software-sheet/1`). It holds the status, and each requirement with its state, who can get it (`public`, `on request`, `none`) and, for a local build, its source and what ran kept apart. The sheet is built field by field, so it holds no path, size, variable name, host, or digest of an unpublished file. The catalog entry names the sheet, and readers check its size, its SHA-256 and that it belongs to the snapshot.

data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Dependabot's pull requests now merge by themselves once CI passes, as in key4hep/k4Bench.

- `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` (the same as k4Bench's): on each pull request opened by dependabot, it enables auto-merge with squash.
- Repository settings, already changed: **Allow auto-merge** is on, and a ruleset **Require CI on main** requires the checks `lint`, `test` and `dashboard` before anything merges into `main` (bypass: the repository's maintainer, as in k4Bench). data.author: jbeirer

data.title: The dashboard's route is reachable from outside CERN
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
The dashboard at https://k4opt-dashboard.app.cern.ch answered only inside CERN: the CERN OpenShift routers admit only CERN's networks unless a route empties its IP whitelist. k4Bench's route does (`haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist: ""`, k4Bench #35); ours carried no annotation.

- `openshift/route.yaml`: the empty whitelist.
- `docs/dashboard.md`: the route is open to the Internet; what the dashboard shows is public, as before.
- `tests/unit/test_deployment.py`: checks the annotation instead of its absence.

The deploy workflow applies the route on merge, so no manual `oc` step is needed. Once deployed, check from outside CERN that the page loads.
